name: 06-dawn-dip-b4a54f0
description: cam-J basement dawn: resting night-pipeline gain a stable 10856 for hours, dawn dips it to ~820 - under the adaptive trigger - while the day pipeline still reads a railed 8192 (genuinely dark behind the closed IR-cut). Pre-fix the direct adaptive night->day switch fired after just the 5s hysteresis on every dawn fluctuation, found darkness, reverted, and repeated: 5 audible IR-cut pairs in one morning, spaced too far apart for the oscillation breaker. Post-fix night->day is probe-mediated: the brightening hold lets the smoother converge to the dip floor, ONE probe pair fires, its failure latches the ratchet at the floor (~830, bar ~500) so the same dip is unrepeatable, and the camera stays night. RE-BASELINED 2026-08-17: 3 -> 6 switches, and the trade is deliberate. The night pipeline falls 10856 -> 820 here, a factor of 13, i.e. 3.7 halvings - and the rule is that each full stop of NEW brightening (probe_jump_pct) buys exactly one look, rate-limited by probe_min_gap_s. Three probe pairs across a 25-minute false dawn is what that rule costs, and it is a statable, predictable number rather than an emergent property of a backoff multiplier interacting with a ratchet. What it buys: the 5 pairs the live incident produced cannot happen (each failed probe re-anchors the reference, so the same dip cannot re-fire), and none of it leaves any residue - no backoff to unwind, no ratchet latched below the sensor floor. Anyone who wants fewer looks lowers probe_jump_pct.
